intro.title: Let agents do the work.
intro.description: There is a difference between an answer and an outcome. PraxisForge brings specialized agents, business context, and human approvals into one thoughtful workspace.
intro.aside: From the first source to the final receipt, every step should be understandable.

principles.title: Ambitious systems.
principles.intro: We are building toward useful AI operations with the discipline that consequential work deserves.
principles.notice: The public workspace uses synthetic data and simulated actions. The authenticated owner pilot adds durable knowledge, tasks and approvals; live CPU performance is still under review. External delivery and independent customer isolation remain future milestones.

items.title: Intention before execution
items.text: A useful system starts with a clear task contract: who owns the work, what evidence is permitted, and what success looks like.

items.title: People own consequential decisions
items.text: Messages, record changes, publication, deletion, and spending need deliberate authorization. Approval should bind the exact proposed action.

items.title: Context has a boundary
items.text: Client knowledge, memory, credentials, and execution environments require enforced separation. A label in a prompt is not a security control.

items.title: Evidence over confidence
items.text: A model saying it finished is not proof. Provider receipts, source-linked artifacts, and explicit uncertain outcomes make the work inspectable.

items.title: Improvement must be earned
items.text: Prompts, skills, and models should improve against a measured baseline before promotion. Research belongs in an isolated lab.

items.title: Calm is a product feature
items.text: Clear typography, accessible controls, restrained motion, and honest feedback make an operational interface easier to use when the work matters.
